note:
Neither passage identifies a botanical species.

Root (2026-11-21): Filed under the geminate דרר as a reduplicated form (dar-dar), as עַפְעַף is to עוף; how the thistle's sense connects to the root is not clear.
summary: Genesis names the thistle alongside the thorn among the weeds the ground produces. Hosea uses the same pair to describe the growth that will cover Israel’s altars.

senses.definition: A prickly weed that grows on the land. The singular can refer collectively to thistles.

evidence.note: The ground brings forth both קוֹץ and דַּרְדַּר as the man labors for food.
Thorns and thistles grow over the altars when the high places are destroyed.
